instruction: Check available flights from Los Angeles to San Francisco for tomorrow.

metadata.explanation: Variation uses same Delta.com website with different airport pair (LAX to SFO) for tomorrow. Reuses existing getter 'get_active_tab_html_parse' and metric 'check_direct_json_object' which parse Delta's flight search results HTML. Airport codes LAX and SFO are standard IATA codes. Task complexity remains identical to original.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator logic can semantically verify the flight search instruction
Getter 'get_active_tab_html_parse' correctly extracts departure airport (start), arrival airport (end), and date (time) from Delta.com flight search results using CSS class selectors
Metric 'check_direct_json_object' correctly compares extracted data against expected values
Expected values use 'get_rule_relativeTime' to dynamically calculate tomorrow's date with proper timezone handling, ensuring verification works across different timezones
Coverage is complete: checks LAX departure, SFO arrival, and tomorrow's date - all requirements from instruction
Minor issue: Missing postconfig to ensure flight search results page is actually loaded before verification - getter assumes active tab is on the results page
Minor issue: Relies on Delta.com-specific CSS classes (mach-flight-context-info__wrapper--date, mach-flight-context-info__wrapper__info--separator) which may break if website structure changes
Note: The rule_validation_issues error message is misleading - using expected.type='rule' with relativeTime is actually the correct configuration pattern for dynamic date calculation
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Add postconfig to re-navigate to flight search results page or verify the active tab URL contains expected flight search patterns before extraction
Consider adding error handling in case CSS selectors don't match (current implementation returns empty strings which would fail the check)
The rule validation error is a false positive - expected.type='rule' is correct when using get_rule_relativeTime. The configuration is semantically valid.
